record.title: Peñas Blancas trucker blockade over shortened transit permission, April–May 2020
record.scope: Truck passage at Peñas Blancas international crossing
record.direction: Truck entry and exit at the Costa Rican crossing obstructed.
record.movement: Cross-border freight trucks, including perishable and urgent goods.
record.exceptions: Passenger and pedestrian access not established by these sources.
record.imposing_authority: Central American freight drivers protesting on the Costa Rican side
record.enforcement: Drivers physically prevented truck passage; police negotiated removal.
record.consequences: Freight held at the crossing; no unverified loss estimate retained.
record.relationship: Separate from AM025 passenger entry policy, AM032 May 18 freight closure, R3-AM-009 March 2019 fees protest and R3-AM-004 October 2020 protest.
record.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
record.official_rationale: Drivers opposed a new maximum 72-hour stay to enter, unload, reload and leave Costa Rica.
record.context: A pandemic transport rule triggered a non-state blockade before the separate May 18 interstate freight dispute.
record.uncertainty: The onset is morning April 30, without exact hour. Police reported normal entry and exit after removal around 05:00 on May 1. The record concerns freight, not a universal passenger closure.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated actual reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Freight blockade from April 30 morning to May 1 morning; eligible only for the stated freight category. No exact hours computed.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Local report and police account confirm deliberate truck blockade.
May 1 about 05:00 removal; minister confirms trucks entering and leaving normally.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The blockade opposed a commercial stay limit imposed during the pandemic. It is coded as a transport protest, not infection control. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Truck drivers opposed reduced permitted stay; no additional rationale inferred.
Peñas Blancas freight, not universal passenger closure.
Two operational accounts support scoped one-calendar-day interval.
